Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI over alleged trade secrets has been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, replacing the magistrate judge who was originally assigned to the case. Here are the details.

New judge means October hearing cancelled

When civil lawsuits are filed in the Northern District of California, they are randomly assigned to either a federal district judge or a magistrate judge. If the case is assigned to a magistrate judge, all parties must state whether they consent to having that judge handle the case with full authority.

This is because district judges have the authority to oversee federal civil cases from start to finish, whereas magistrate judges must obtain consent from all parties before they can handle a case with full authority.

On the day Apple filed its trade secrets lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and Jony Ive's io Products, the case was randomly assigned to Magistrate Judge Virginia K. DeMarchi.

This arrangement meant that all parties in the lawsuit had to submit forms stating whether they consented to Judge DeMarchi handling the case with full authority.

Apple appears to have rejected this arrangement. Apple filed a consent or declination statement yesterday (which is not yet publicly available), and this document appears to have triggered the process of reassigning the case to a district judge.

No other document can be seen that would explain this reassignment, which strongly suggests Apple struck out the option to decline the magistrate judge's jurisdiction.

As a result, the case has now been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, with Magistrate Judge Nathanael Cousins handling discovery-related matters.

With the reassignment, the initial case management conference originally scheduled for October 13 before Judge DeMarchi has been cancelled and needs to be rescheduled before Judge Davila.

However, two other sets of deadlines remain unchanged: parties must meet to discuss settlement and a discovery plan by September 22, then submit initial disclosures and a joint case management statement by October 6.
